video.title: Fastest Way to Copy Winning Digital Products (Picsart)

summary: Chris Koerner shows how to find and copy winning digital products on Etsy. The old-school method sorts printables by top reviews and looks for sellers with many reviews but few products, cross-checked on Google Trends. The faster hack changes 'star' to 'best' in the Etsy filter URL to reveal hidden best-sellers. He then uses Picsart's AI enhance and image generation to create similar designs, tests them on Facebook Marketplace or $20 Facebook ads, and moves winners to Etsy. The key takeaway is to copy what already works and change nothing at first.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; presents solo screen-share tutorial

ideas.name: Copycat Etsy digital printables using AI image tools
ideas.one_liner: Reverse engineer Etsy best-selling printables, generate similar designs with Picsart AI, and sell them as instant downloads on Etsy.
ideas.business_model: One-off digital product sales (instant download printables) on Etsy, net of Etsy fees
ideas.customer: Etsy shoppers buying printables: wall art, junk journals, baby shower games, coloring pages, stickers, homework pages
ideas.problem: Digital product markets are crowded, so sellers waste months on products with too much supply and too little demand
ideas.offer: Printable designs closely modelled on proven best-sellers, with AI-generated variations (e.g. seasonal wall art such as an Easter bunny)

pricing.model: Per-download price set near the proven best-seller; not specified
pricing.notes: No specific price given; the baby shower game price is only a guessing game in the video

acquisition_channels.details: List on Etsy and use Etsy's own search; use Etsy Ads on printables since the only cost is time/ad spend against a near-zero marginal product cost; optionally buy an established Etsy account whose feedback the algorithm already favours.

quote.text: you can buy Etsy accounts that have established feedback you're not necessarily buying a full store or a business or anything
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Test designs on Facebook Marketplace: list five designs with the same title, price and description as a pure A/B test and compare views, clicks and messages.

quote.text: Facebook Marketplace is the best place to test concepts like this because you could take five rabbit designs like these
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Run Facebook ads at a $20 budget each with the same ad but a different design, then move the winning design to Etsy.

quote.text: use that to launch some Facebook ads $20 budget each same ad different design see what people are clicking on
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Digital instant download. Designs are created in Picsart using AI enhance and AI image generation, using a best-seller screenshot as the style reference, then listed with multiple mock-up pictures. Delivery to the buyer is automatic via Etsy.
unit_economics_claims: Top Etsy printable sellers show 175,000 to 462,000 sales
Etsy Ads cost to acquire a customer is bounded by product price less Etsy fees
Four to six hours of research suggested to find winning categories
ideas.startup_cost: Low: Etsy listing fees, a Picsart subscription, a $20 per design ad test; exact figures not stated

acquisition.how: Etsy search, Etsy Ads and Facebook ads are inbound and software-run, so agents can do most of it. Research scraping can be done by agents (Manus/Operator), but the Etsy URL hack may be fragile and Etsy's terms may restrict scraping.

onboarding.how: Buyers purchase and download instantly with no onboarding.

delivery.how: AI generates designs and listing images, and Etsy delivers the files. A human or vision-checked review is needed for quality, text errors and copyright similarity.

support.how: Low volume of buyer messages and refund questions; an agent can handle most with occasional human approval.

uk_applicability.notes: Etsy operates in the UK and sellers can list digital goods. UK VAT on digital sales needs handling (Etsy collects VAT in many cases), and HMRC trading income must be declared. Seasonal holidays differ (e.g. Easter works, Thanksgiving does not).

risks: Copying designs closely risks copyright or IP infringement claims and Etsy takedowns
Buying Etsy accounts likely breaches Etsy terms and can lead to suspension
The URL trick to reveal best-sellers may stop working
AI struggles with text in images
Review counts are a proxy for sales, not a guarantee

tactics.name: Old-school Etsy reverse engineering via reviews
steps: Search 'printable' on Etsy and filter to instant download
Sort by top reviews and open the top few listings in separate tabs
Prefer sellers with thousands of reviews but few products (e.g. under about 2,000 SKUs)
Check the category on Google Trends over 5 years to confirm growth
Discard items from sellers with huge catalogues or declining trends

quote.text: finding a seller that has a rare combination of thousands of reviews but not a lot of products those are the diamonds in the rough
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Etsy best-seller URL hack
steps: Search a term such as 'printable' on Etsy
Open All Filters and tick Star Sellers
In the results URL replace the word 'star' with 'best'
Browse the resulting best-sellers and open the store to see total sales
Optionally use ChatGPT Operator or Manus to scrape best-selling products and stores

quote.text: go to the URL and replace the word star with the word best and look all the products change now now you have best sellers
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Create a variation with Picsart AI
steps: Save or screenshot the best-selling listing image
Upload to Picsart and use AI enhance to improve quality and remove watermarks where possible
Use the AI image generator with a prompt (e.g. rabbit in grass) and the uploaded image as style reference
Pick the best generated options and list them

quote.text: use PixArt and their AI generation tools to come up with some other designs for yourself
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Cheap demand testing before Etsy
steps: List about five design variants on Facebook Marketplace with identical title, description and price
Compare views, clicks and messages per listing
Alternatively run Facebook ads at $20 per design with identical copy
Move the winning design to Etsy

quote.text: you could list all five of them in the exact same market with the exact same description a pure AB test
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Copy first, change later
steps: Copy the existing winning business as closely as possible at the start
Change nothing until your own data shows what to improve
Optimise gradually and differentiate later

quote.text: I'm going to start by 100% copying the existing business because everything I change increases the likelihood that I'll have suboptimal success
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use marketplace social proof (reviews and sales counts) as free demand data before building anything.
The best targets combine high sales with a small catalogue, which suggests a few winning products rather than a broad shotgun approach.
Validate demand with cheap A/B tests on Facebook Marketplace or about $20 of ads before investing in a full catalogue.
Cross-check marketplace popularity with Google Trends to avoid declining niches.
In the early stage, copy proven formats exactly and only change things once your own data justifies it.

quote.text: copy what works change nothing eventually you'll find things to change but don't change in the beginning
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: AI tools can cut design production for digital goods to minutes, so product creation is no longer the bottleneck; finding demand is.
Seasonal products let you reuse the same research and generation workflow for each upcoming holiday.
Marketplace-specific quirks such as hidden filters can give a research edge but may disappear, so do not build a business that depends on them.

evidence_quality.rationale: A short tutorial with no first-hand sales results. All sales and review figures belong to other Etsy sellers and are read from screens. The method is concrete and reproducible but unproven by the speaker, and IP and platform-rule risks are not covered.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host says he has no course to sell. He promotes a Facebook ad guide linked in the notes and appears to feature Picsart, which may be a sponsor or affiliate relationship, though this is not stated.
